newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee may rise, but uptrend still shallow.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee may rise, but uptrend still shallow.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE coffee futures may motor higher on Friday to extend recent gains although in the short term the uptrend is still shallow, technical analysts said.
Traders called the market to open a hefty $100 higher after another sharp rally in New York on Thursday saw prices rocketing to the highest level in almost three years.
But in practice London might open $50-$60 up.
New York's arabica futures rocketed to new life of contract highs across-the-board on Thursday, as concern about tight prompt supplies fuelled speculative buying.
July jumped 12.50 cents per lb -- or nearly six percent -- to finish at 222.90 cents, after ranging between a new lifetime high of 224.00 and 210.00.

Analysts attributed the market's recent surge -- which has seen the May contract soar by 36.40 cents, or about 17 percent, since last Friday -- to a drawdown in stocks of coffee certified for delivery against the exchange.
London's robusta futures, trailing New York, ended Thursday with pared gains on overhead origin sales.
On the charts the robusta market looked neutral to potentially bullish in the long term, said Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst.
But she said in the short run the uptrend was rather shallow.
July has been trading between $1,705 and $1,546 since early April.
Immediate support was seen intact at $1,660 and the next upper layer of support was at $1,620.
Nearby resistance was pegged at $1,690 although the more critical ones are at $1,705, followed by $1,715, $1,720 and probably $1,740.
The ultimate upside objective was the March 21 peak of $1,820.
